criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Official Purdue GIS historical PMU feature 278 (1935-36) aligns the structural shell bounds to within about 0.5 m on the main outline.
GIS feature 482 (1938-40) is consistent in broad plan but extends ~4 m farther north; phases and later additions make this comparison uncertain.
findings: Identity is supported by GIS name/phase and recognizable tower/wings.
The evidence is historical and not a current survey; complete present-day footprint and courtyard shape are not fully validated.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: Read-only master marker reports one expected PMU instance at (205.75,-271.65,0), zero rotation, unit scale, and expected linked asset path.
The local structural bounds align with the historical GIS outline under the project’s approximate local conversion.
findings: Placement and transform are directly confirmed; exact orientation and dimensions have no current survey/control source.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Fresh-reopened asset bounds are Z 0-29.5 m; repeated belt levels and several wing/tower roofs are present.
Render evidence shows a multi-level central tower and lower wings.
findings: No measured height, floor schedule, or roof/elevation source was available; 29.5 m is only the model’s own extent.
The broad pale roof masses are simplified and their profiles are not supported by a measured/source elevation.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: Controlled south, west, and oblique renders show the clock tower, wings, brick/limestone treatment, repeated windows, and Gothic-like ornament.
Official Purdue archival imagery supports a central tower and adjoining wings as identity cues.
findings: The silhouette is recognizable, but many windows read as simple rectangles rather than the tall arched openings suggested by imagery.
Main entrance and facade stonework are weakly articulated; repeated flat wall treatment and pale roofs reduce fidelity.
Interior props are present, but no source-backed interior plan was available to verify their layout.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Fresh reopen confirms 414 objects in the expected asset file/collection and an identity local root.
All mesh objects have assigned materials; material nodes are procedural and no external image dependency was found.
Read-only master inspection confirms one linked placement marker at the expected manifest transform.
findings: The standalone asset is portable based on current inspection.

At review time the project did not provide a PMU-specific builder source/build script, preview/evidence record, or validation log; the current independent audit artifacts document this review but do not replace build provenance.
